citation: Das S, Anczukow O, Akerman M, Krainer AR. Oncogenic splicing factor SRSF1 is a critical transcriptional target of MYC. Cell Reports. 2012. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2011.12.001.
description: This paper shows that altered SRSF1 abundance is sufficient to change alternative splicing of a defined subset of transcripts. It supports a target-specific bridge from SRSF1 perturbation to RNA-processing changes, but not the exact neuronal mRNA-abundance signature in this screen.

citation: Chen L, Luo C, Shen L, Liu Y, Wang Q, Zhang C, et al. SRSF1 prevents DNA damage and promotes tumorigenesis through regulation of DBF4B pre-mRNA splicing. Cell Reports. 2017. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2017.11.091.
description: The study connects SRSF1 inactivation to a specific splicing defect that increases DNA damage in colorectal cancer cells. It was used as indirect support for stress-like components in the Srsf1 signatures.

citation: Gavin JM, Hoar K, Xu Q, Ma J, Lin Y, Chen J, et al. Mechanistic study of Uba5 enzyme and the Ufm1 conjugation pathway. Journal of Biological Chemistry. 2014. doi:10.1074/jbc.M114.573972.
description: This biochemical and cellular paper establishes UBA5 as the E1 that activates UFM1 and transfers it to UFC1. It supplies the direct target-to-UFMylation step used to interpret Uba5 perturbations.

citation: Xie Z, Fang Z, Pan Z. Ufl1/RCAD, a Ufm1 E3 ligase, has an intricate connection with ER stress. International Journal of Biological Macromolecules. 2019. doi:10.1016/j.ijbiomac.2019.05.170.
description: This review summarizes evidence that the UBA5-UFC1-UFM1-UFL1 UFMylation cascade is tied to ER homeostasis and ER-stress signaling. It supports an indirect Uba5-to-ER-stress bridge.

citation: Kosillo P, Doig NM, Ahmed KM, Agopyan-Miu AHCW, Wong CD, Conyers L, et al. Tsc1-mTORC1 signaling controls striatal dopamine release and cognitive flexibility. Nature Communications. 2019. doi:10.1038/s41467-019-13396-8.
description: Cell-type-specific Tsc1 deletion in mouse dopamine neurons constitutively activated mTORC1 and changed neuronal physiology. It gives direct neuronal evidence that Tsc1 loss derepresses mTORC1, while leaving this screen's exact lysosomal and sterol transcripts as an indirect consequence.

citation: Karalis V, Caval-Holme F, Bateup HS. Raptor downregulation rescues neuronal phenotypes in mouse models of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex. Nature Communications. 2022. doi:10.1038/s41467-022-31961-6.
description: This genetic-rescue study shows that reducing the mTORC1 component Raptor rebalances signaling and improves phenotypes in Tsc1-knockout neurons. It supports interpreting Tsc1 perturbation effects through neuronal mTORC1 activation.

citation: Mattison KA, Tossing G, Mulroe F, Simmons C, Butler KM, Schreiber A, et al. ATP6V0C variants impair V-ATPase function causing a neurodevelopmental disorder often associated with epilepsy. Brain. 2023. doi:10.1093/brain/awac330.
description: Human ATP6V0C variants and ATP6V0C knockdown in model organisms impaired V-ATPase function and neuronal behavior. The paper supports a specific bridge from ATP6V0C loss to V-ATPase dysfunction.

citation: Xu Y, Zhou P, Cheng S, Lu Q, Nowak K, Hopp AK, Li L, et al. A bacterial effector reveals the V-ATPase-ATG16L1 axis that initiates xenophagy. Cell. 2019. doi:10.1016/j.cell.2019.06.007.
description: A host-factor CRISPR screen identified V-ATPase and the ATP6V0C Gln124 site as critical for ATG16L1 recruitment during vacuolar-damage autophagy. It supports an ATP6V0C-to-autophagy bridge but not the direction of the screen's paralog or neuronal stress transcripts.

citation: Tan ZW, Fei G, Paulo JA, Bellaousov S, Martin SES, Duveau DY, et al. O-GlcNAc regulates gene expression by controlling detained intron splicing. Nucleic Acids Research. 2020. doi:10.1093/nar/gkaa263.
description: Manipulating O-GlcNAc cycling changed detained-intron splicing and system-wide gene expression. It provides a target-specific OGT/O-GlcNAc bridge to RNA-processing changes, but not exact directions for the neuronal genes measured here.

citation: Ramirez DH, Yang B, D'Souza AK, Shen D, Woo CM. Truncation of the TPR domain of OGT alters substrate and glycosite selection. Analytical and Bioanalytical Chemistry. 2021. doi:10.1007/s00216-021-03731-8.
description: Perturbing the OGT TPR domain changed O-GlcNAc modification of proteins, with the largest changes among proteins involved in mRNA splicing. This supports an OGT-to-splicing-protein bridge for Ogt signatures enriched in RNA-processing genes.

citation: Bridi M, Schoch H, Florian C, Poplawski SG, Banerjee A, Hawk JD, et al. Transcriptional corepressor SIN3A regulates hippocampal synaptic plasticity via Homer1/mGluR5 signaling. JCI Insight. 2020. doi:10.1172/jci.insight.92385.
description: Postnatal neuronal Sin3a deletion increased Homer1 expression and altered synaptic plasticity in mouse hippocampus. It documents that SIN3A acts as a neuronal transcriptional corepressor, while the screen mostly reports other genes and regions.

citation: Salas-Armenteros I, Perez-Calero C, Bayona-Feliu A, Tumini E, Luna R, Aguilera A. Human THO-Sin3A interaction reveals new mechanisms to prevent R-loops that cause genome instability. EMBO Journal. 2017. doi:10.15252/embj.201797208.
description: The paper shows that the human THO/TREX complex physically and functionally interacts with the SIN3A HDAC complex to suppress R-loops, DNA damage, and replication impairment. It supports an indirect bridge between Sin3a or Thoc1 loss and RNA-processing/genome-stress responses.

citation: Dejosez M, Levine SS, Frampton GM, Whyte WA, Stratton SA, Barton MC, et al. Ronin/Hcf-1 binds to a hyperconserved enhancer element and regulates genes involved in the growth of embryonic stem cells. Genes and Development. 2010. doi:10.1101/gad.1935210.
description: Ronin/THAP11 with HCF-1 binds a conserved element at genes involved in transcription initiation, mRNA splicing, and metabolism in embryonic stem cells. It supplies a direct THAP11 transcriptional-regulatory bridge, but the neuronal downstream transcripts in this dataset are not documented targets.

citation: Maertens GN, Cook NJ, Wang W, Hare S, Gupta SS, Oztop I, et al. Structural basis for nuclear import of splicing factors by human Transportin 3. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America. 2014. doi:10.1073/pnas.1320755111.
description: This structural study shows that TNPO3 recognizes phosphorylated RS domains and imports SR-domain splicing factors. It supports a target-specific bridge from Tnpo3 perturbation to splicing-factor localization and RNA processing.

citation: Dominguez-Sanchez MS, Barroso S, Gomez-Gonzalez B, Luna R, Aguilera A. Genome instability and transcription elongation impairment in human cells depleted of THO/TREX. PLoS Genetics. 2011. doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1002386.
description: Human THO/TREX depletion, including THOC1 depletion, impaired transcription elongation and mRNA export and increased R-loop-dependent genome instability. It supports a THOC1-to-RNA-processing and genome-stress bridge.
